question: The coordinates of the vertices of a triangle are A(0,0), B(8,0), and C(0,6). What is the location of the orthocenter?
solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ For any **right-angled triangle**, the **orthocenter** (the point where all three altitudes intersect) always lies exactly at the **vertex** containing the **right angle** (90°). In the triangle with vertices **A(0, 0)**, **B(8, 0)**, and **C(0, 6)**, side AB lies on the x-axis and side AC lies on the y-axis. Since the x-axis and y-axis are **perpendicular** at the **origin**, the right angle is formed at vertex **A(0, 0)**. Therefore, the orthocenter is **(0, 0)**. **∴ The correct answer is (0, 0).**
